findings.title: TopicsController#unsubscribe crashes when TopicUser record is absent
findings.body: `tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` can return nil for a user who received a notification (e.g. was @-mentioned or quoted) but has never actually visited the topic, because TopicUser rows are only created on visit/track. The very next line then dereferences `tu.notification_level`, raising NoMethodError on nil and producing a 500 for those users right when they click the unsubscribe link in an email — exactly the users the feature is meant to serve. The controller should use TopicUser.change (which upserts), or explicitly check for nil and create the record with the new notification level.

findings.title: List-Unsubscribe header still points at global preferences, not the per-topic URL
findings.body: In `header_args`, the RFC8058 one-click `List-Unsubscribe` header is set to `template_args[:user_preferences_url]` even though `@opts[:unsubscribe_url]` (the new per-topic URL, which is the entire point of this PR) is now available and merged into `template_args`. Mail clients such as Gmail, Apple Mail and Outlook honor this header to render a one-click "Unsubscribe" button; users who click it will be sent to the global preferences page and effectively unsubscribed from all email, not just this topic. The header should use `template_args[:unsubscribe_url]` when present, so the standard one-click path matches the in-body link.

findings.title: GET endpoint mutates a user's notification level with no CSRF protection or signed token
findings.body: `TopicsController#unsubscribe` is wired as a GET route (`get "t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe" => "topics#unsubscribe"`) and silently calls `tu.save!` to change the logged-in user's notification level. The `ensure_logged_in` filter only requires a session; it provides no CSRF defense, and there is no signed token in the URL analogous to the existing `email/unsubscribe/:key` mechanism. Any third-party site can embed `` and, when a logged-in Discourse user loads the page, their topic notification state is changed without consent. State-changing actions triggered from email should either use a signed, single-use key (as the global email unsubscribe already does) or be a POST guarded by a CSRF token / explicit confirmation step.

findings.title: Toggle logic only mutes users already at regular; watching/tracking users keep getting emails
findings.body: The branch `if tu.notification_level > TopicUser.notification_levels[:regular]` sets the level to `:regular` for users at `:tracking` or `:watching`, and only sets `:muted` for users already at `:regular` or `:muted`. With the notification levels enum (muted=0, regular=1, tracking=2, watching=3), a user who was watching the topic and clicks unsubscribe is downgraded to `regular`, which still produces email notifications for every reply. The user-visible text in `topic.unsubscribe.stop_notifications` says "You will stop receiving notifications", which is false for that common case. The action should either jump straight to `:muted` (matching the wording) or clearly document that the first click is a "reduce" and the second is a "mute".

findings.title: Misspelled identifier `stopNotificiationsText`
findings.body: The computed property is named `stopNotificiationsText` (three i's, 'Notificiations') in the controller, and the same misspelling is hard-coded in `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs` line 3 (`{{{stopNotificiationsText}}}`). It currently works because the two misspellings match, but any future search/rename for `stopNotificationsText` will miss this, and the misspelling will be baked into the public template API. The identifier should be corrected in both files (and the template updated) before this ships.

findings.title: Test for List-Unsubscribe header only checks presence, not that the per-topic URL is used
findings.body: The existing test `it "has an List-Unsubscribe header"` only asserts that the header is `be_present`, even though the new test setup now passes `unsubscribe_url: "/t/1234/unsubscribe"`. Because the assertion doesn't compare the header value, it would still pass if the header were (incorrectly) hard-coded to the global preferences URL. The test should assert that `header_args['List-Unsubscribe']` includes the per-topic `unsubscribe_url`, so the regression in `message_builder.rb#header_args` is caught.
